title: Multiple keys that show up as "Undefined" and can only be mapped to one key

status.label: Potential JIS key identity collision
status.detail: The reporter found three distinct JIS keys that Windows reports as VK 255; current remap lookup is keyed by virtual key, but a current-build retest is still needed.

next_action.label: Retest distinct JIS keys on a current build
next_action.reason: Confirm the VK 255 collision still occurs, then design scan-code identity support without changing ordinary virtual-key remaps.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed JIS key list, the VK 255 check with Keyboard Manager turned off, and the registry scan-code workaround. Could you confirm whether the same three keys still collide on PowerToys v0.102.3001 or newer with the same Japanese PS/2 keyboard? If they do, please confirm the Windows version and whether each key still reports VK 255; there is no need to resend the workaround already included here.

judgment.rationale: The report identifies multiple distinct physical JIS keys that collapse to VK 255 even with Keyboard Manager disabled. Current Keyboard Manager single-key remaps are looked up by vkCode, so the shared virtual key explains why those sources collide. A scan-code-aware identity for otherwise indistinguishable keys is a concrete candidate, subject to a current-build retest and careful compatibility coverage.
evidence: The report identifies a Fujitsu JIS 106/109 keyboard on Windows 10 22H2 and distinguishes the Henkan, Hiragana/Katakana, and Yen keys by PS/2 scan codes 0x79, 0x70, and 0x7d.
The reporter says those three keys all appear as Undefined and cannot be assigned separately, while Muhenkan (VK 235) and backslash/underscore (VK 193) can be mapped individually.
In a 2023 comment, the reporter says KeyboardStateView showed key code 255 for the affected keys while Keyboard Manager was off, and supplied a registry Scan Code Mapper workaround.

Current upstream at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 uses data->lParam->vkCode for the runtime single-key lookup in KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp and keys MappingConfiguration::singleKeyReMap by originalKey; scanMap is only consulted for the special numpad-with-Shift path.
No linked fixing pull request appears in the saved issue timeline; the last discussion comment supplied an AutoHotkey workaround rather than a PowerToys fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Retest the three reported JIS keys on a current build; if they still arrive with the same VK 255 but distinct scan codes, design scan-code-aware source identity for those keys and add regression coverage for existing virtual-key mappings.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current event lookup and configuration table are keyed by virtual key, matching the reported collision. A scan-code-aware identity could distinguish the affected physical keys, but current hardware behavior and compatibility requirements remain to be verified.

proposed_fixes.title: Distinguish JIS keys that share VK 255
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The keyboard driver reports several distinct JIS keys as VK 255, while Keyboard Manager stores and looks up source remaps by virtual key. The low-level keyboard event also carries scan-code data, but the normal single-key remap path does not use it as part of source identity.
plan: Retest the reported Henkan, Hiragana/Katakana, and Yen keys on a current supported build and record their low-level virtual-key and scan-code values.
Extend source-key identity and settings serialization to distinguish otherwise identical undefined virtual keys by scan code, while preserving the existing virtual-key path for ordinary keys.
Update the editor to present distinct stable labels for those keys and reject duplicate mappings only when both source identities match.
Add tests for distinct scan codes sharing VK 255, duplicate identical sources, settings save/reload, extended scan-code handling, and unaffected standard virtual-key mappings.
verification: On a JIS keyboard, the three reported keys can be assigned different targets and each triggers only its own mapping.
The mappings survive a Keyboard Manager settings save/reload.
Existing virtual-key remaps, including the reported VK 235 and VK 193 cases, continue to behave unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The reporter's VK 255 observation and current virtual-key-only lookup strongly support the collision mechanism, but current hardware values and scan-code compatibility have not been retested.

issue_context.summary: On a Japanese JIS keyboard, several distinct physical keys are reported as VK 255 and therefore cannot be remapped independently in Keyboard Manager.
known_information: The original report identifies a Fujitsu Japanese PS/2 106/109 keyboard on US English Windows 10 22H2 and PowerToys 0.70.1.
The reporter lists distinct PS/2 scan codes for Henkan (0x79), Hiragana/Katakana (0x70), and Yen (0x7d), and says all three appear as Undefined and share one remap.
The reporter says KeyboardStateView showed key code 255 with Keyboard Manager disabled, and posted a registry scan-code workaround.
Current upstream at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 keys the normal single-key remap lookup by vkCode; scan codes are used only by a separate numpad-with-Shift handling path.
inferences: If the distinct scan codes are still delivered on a current build, using scan code as part of the source identity for VK 255 keys could make those keys independently mappable.
The reporter's AutoHotkey workaround shows that scan-code-level remapping can work on that setup, but does not establish PowerToys compatibility requirements or current behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The report provides unusually specific hardware, scan-code, virtual-key, and workaround evidence. Current source confirms that the standard remap table cannot distinguish two keys with the same vkCode. A narrowly gated scan-code identity for otherwise undefined keys is plausible, but must be checked against current device events, settings persistence, extended scan codes, and ordinary key mappings.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and all five comments, including the VK 255 observation, registry workaround, and AutoHotkey workaround.
Checked the saved issue timeline for a linked fixing pull request; none was present.

Inspected MappingConfiguration::AddSingleKeyRemap and KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368: normal mappings are keyed and looked up by virtual key, with scan-code use limited to numpad/Shift handling.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same three JIS keys still collide as VK 255 on a current PowerToys build, and the current Windows/keyboard-driver version
information_gaps.why_needed: The report and code evidence are strong but old; a current result confirms the behavior and whether the same scan-code design applies.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest separate remaps for Henkan, Hiragana/Katakana, and Yen on PowerToys v0.102.3001 or newer with the same JIS keyboard; confirm whether each still appears as VK 255.
